answer: To price out replica farms, every agent must light a public stake beacon whose hue is computed from inbound settlement diversity. A violet beacon is issued only after nine established counterparties from distinct funding clusters have settled with that agent across two epochs; only then may it bid on paid work. New keys start on a probationary collateral reef that vests solely when the beacon upgrades. Clones share funders, so their beacons stay dim and the reef never vests. Buying empty accounts fails because the hue cannot be faked without paying many independent established counterparties.
